package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised by a malicious developer who injected JavaScript code into the Tornado Cash UI, causing users’ private deposit notes to be exfiltrated to an unauthorized external server. This enabled the attacker to steal funds from users by obtaining the cryptographic secrets required to withdraw assets from the platform.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user interacts with the deposit or withdrawal functionality in the web UI
execution_context.file_location: JavaScript frontend code, specifically within modules handling deposit/withdrawal logic (e.g., deposit.js, withdraw.js, or main UI logic files)
required_permissions: Access to in-browser sensitive data (user's private deposit notes)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user generates or uses a deposit note, the code accesses the user's private deposit note, serializes it, and sends it via an HTTPS POST request to an attacker-controlled external server, resulting in exfiltration of cryptographic credentials and enabling theft of user funds.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses highly sensitive cryptographic secrets (deposit notes) and transmits them to an external, unauthorized domain without user consent. This behavior directly enables theft of funds and is never required for legitimate operation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or cryptographic secrets outside the user's browser or to any server, as all privacy-preserving operations are intended to be local. Any such transmission is a severe violation of user trust and protocol security.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or error reporting may send non-sensitive usage data, but never private cryptographic secrets such as deposit notes. There is no valid reason for deposit notes to leave the user's browser.
key_indicators: Direct access to in-browser cryptographic secrets (deposit notes)
Network request (POST) to a non-official, attacker-controlled domain
Sensitive data (deposit note) serialized and transmitted externally
No user notification or consent for exfiltration of secrets
Code present in deposit/withdrawal logic files that handles sensitive operations

attack_chain.action: Malicious developer commits JavaScript code to the Tornado Cash UI repository, embedding logic to exfiltrate deposit notes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is deployed to the production UI, making it accessible to users.

attack_chain.action: User interacts with the compromised Tornado Cash UI and generates or uses a private deposit note during deposit or withdrawal.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the user's browser during sensitive operations.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code captures the user's private deposit note and sends it to the attacker's server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives deposit notes and is able to reconstruct the cryptographic secrets required to withdraw funds.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the stolen deposit notes to withdraw funds from Tornado Cash, draining affected user accounts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: theft of user funds from the platform.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in the UI accessing or reading deposit notes or other cryptographic secrets in-browser
Network requests (especially POST) from the UI to non-official, external domains during deposit or withdrawal operations
Unexpected serialization and transmission of deposit notes or private keys from the browser
Absence of user notification or consent dialogs when sensitive data is transmitted externally
file_indicators: Modifications or additions to main UI JavaScript files responsible for deposit/withdrawal logic (e.g., deposit.js, withdraw.js, main.js)
Presence of code referencing or calling external domains not associated with tornado.cash or its official infrastructure
New or altered functions that access deposit notes and perform network requests
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from the UI to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., https://attacker-server.com/collect) not associated with tornado.cash
Unusual outbound traffic from user browsers during deposit or withdrawal operations, especially to unknown domains
Network requests containing serialized deposit notes or cryptographic secrets in the payload
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor the Tornado Cash UI codebase for unauthorized changes that access and transmit deposit notes or other cryptographic secrets. Use browser extension or proxy tools to detect POST requests from the UI to non-official domains, particularly during deposit or withdrawal operations. Audit JavaScript code for any logic that serializes and sends sensitive data externally. Implement allowlisting for network destinations and alert on any network activity from the UI to domains not on the allowlist. Regularly review code diffs for new or modified functions that handle deposit notes and perform network requests.
